name: Nyerere National Park (Selous)
region: Morogoro and Lindi regions, southern Tanzania
tagline: Boat safaris, walking safaris and wild dogs in the Rufiji River wilderness.
highlight: Drifting down the Rufiji River past hippos and crocodiles at dusk.
shortDescription: A huge southern park with the Rufiji River, boat and walking safaris, African wild dogs and fewer visitors than the northern circuit.

image.alt: A scene in Nyerere National Park

intro: Nyerere National Park was carved from the northern part of the former Selous Game Reserve, one of the largest protected areas in Africa. The Rufiji River winds through it, feeding lakes, channels and floodplains where hippos, crocodiles and huge numbers of birds gather.

What sets Nyerere apart is the variety of safari styles. In addition to normal game drives, camps offer boat safaris on Lake Tagalala and the Rufiji, and guided walking safaris with armed rangers, which are not allowed in most other Tanzanian parks. The park is one of the best places in the country to see African wild dogs, along with lions, elephants, giraffes and buffalo.

It is easily reached by a short flight from Dar es Salaam, making it a good add-on for a beach holiday on Zanzibar. Most camps are small, and visitor numbers are low, giving a more private experience than the northern circuit.

whyVisit.intro: Nyerere is a wilder, quieter alternative to the northern parks.
